Rainbow table attacks work by pre-computing hashes for common passwords and comparing them against stolen hash databases. The core idea is that modern password hashing uses cryptographic functions designed to be computationally infeasible to reverse, so you can't just brute-force them. Instead, rainbow tables store pre-computed hash-to-password mappings for millions of common passwords. When someone tries to log in, the system checks if their input hash matches one in the table. If it does, the system authenticates them.
